Kamiensk Jewish Cemetery

Jewish Cemetery · Kamieńsk, Poland

Demolished. Kamieńsk, granted town rights in 1374 as a private town, saw Jewish settlement likely begin at the end of the 18th century; population reached about 42% (856) by 1921. The community, though poor, worked mainly in small trade and crafts. Kamieńsk was nearly destroyed in September 1939, scattering residents to nearby villages; roughly 500 remaining Jews were deported to Treblinka in October 1942. This cemetery's exact founding is unknown, though its oldest tombstone was likely erected in 1831; eyewitnesses recall preserved matzevot as late as 1978. Local authorities later allocated part of the grounds to a road-construction company, with the remainder converted into a sports shooting range that remains active today.
